title.narrative: NCO Mombe YaAmai ITL 2 Round 3: Women Economic Empowerment through Mother's Cow

description.narrative: The project, developed from a 5 months phase 1 learning research (Feb - July 2024), aims to enhance women's economic empowerment and resilience in the dairy and livestock value chain in Mudzi district. It will directly reach 3,000 local farmers, with a primary focus on women and youth, and indirectly benefit 12,000 people. The mother's cow project; riding on existing traditional practice looks to enhance inclusive market systems development. The project phase II will be implemented over 36 months (starting October 2024) and has a robust monitoring, evaluation, and learning framework to share best practices and lessons learned with stakeholders. This project therefore modifies the mother’s cow to include those without, through subsidized in-calf dairy heifers and a dairy bull. Women with existing cows will the targeted for training on maximising the potential of their assets. This prototype targets 2 existing women's groups (producer group cum ISAL), also linked to livestock bush meal enterprises. The primary participants in the project are women small holder farmers in the targeted wards who make a living from the fragile environment. These direct participants comprise women (65%), men (35%) small holder farmers, priority will be given to ensure 30% youth (including young women) representation. The targeting of women (65%) and youth (30%) in the "Mother's Cow" project is a strategic approach to address gender gaps and drive greater economic empowerment and resilience within the local dairy and livestock value chain. By increasing women's ownership, control, and productive use of dairy, beef, and livestock assets, the project aims to enhance household incomes and nutrition security, Research done indicated that women are most likely going to re-invest to reinvest their earnings into family well-being than men. Engaging youth is crucial for the long-term sustainability of the project, as young people are often more receptive to new technologies and innovative approaches, making them vital agents of change in the agricultural sector. Indirect beneficiaries will include household members, locals supplying input, extension and marketing services to the expanded dairy and beef value chain. A simple computer will be placed at the homestead where the cows will be located and women can access platform loaded with knowledge resources such as cow management, health, nutrition and marketing. Women with cows will be contribute in the procurement of laptops. ICT will be used for groups to manage their business on mobile phones and laptops to allow for web and mobile app, whilst information sharing and marketing will be done using WhatsApp Chatbot. The phase I will ascertain the availability of smart phones among women. Basic capacity building on smart phones will be done at community level. Another CAZ faith partner, Silveira House, will envision the women’s groups such that they are able to conceive a future life without poverty.
